Here is a Semgrep rule that matches the vulnerable behavior and avoids matching the patched behavior:

```yaml
id: "vuln-countly-server-2bfa1ee1"
title: "Potential Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password Vulnerability"
description: "This rule checks if a password recovery mechanism is using SHA512 hash function which may be vulnerable to brute force attacks."
severity: WARNING
languages:
  - javascript
metadata:
  tags: ["security", "authentication"]
pattern: >-
  :[
    (
      $ = import("./utils/authorizer.js") ||
      import("./utils/common.js") ||
      import("./plugins/pluginManager.js") ||
      import("./parts/mgmt/mail.js") ||
      import("./parts/data/stats.js") ||
      import("request") ||
      import("url") ||
      import("crypto")
    ) &&
    $["sha512Hash"] &&
    $["sha512Hash"].toString().includes("function sha512Hash")
  ]
```

This rule will match if any of the imported modules in the function call chain contains a `sha512Hash` method. The `sha512Hash` method is assumed to be vulnerable to brute force attacks, as it's used for password recovery without additional security measures.

Please note that this rule might not catch all possible instances of the vulnerability because the function name could be different or imported from a different module. You may need to adjust the pattern accordingly.
